category: Turbobit Turbo-access storefront (reseller domain on the Turbobit platform)

free_tier.stated: None sold here. The site sells 'Turbo access'; the free path it describes is the normal Turbobit one: 'If you do not want to obtain Turbo (premium) access, undergo testing to show that *You are not a robot*, wait during the time-out, and you will receive a link to slow download of the file.'
free_tier.notes: The free path is on turbobit.net, not on this domain.

per_object_cap.stated: 'Up to 100GB file transfer volume' for sharing; the storage total is advertised as unlimited
per_object_cap.notes: The 100 GB figure is described as transfer volume, not a single-object cap; unverified as a hard number.

retention.stated: not stated on the pages that rendered; Turbobit's own FAQ says files are kept while the account is active and longer for premium

egress.terms: 'Turbo access allows you to download files with unlimited speed' - speed, not volume.

interface_detail: Single-page app (data-app="turbobit") whose tariff and checkout pages render entirely from JavaScript; the only readable surfaces are the marketing page and the FAQ.
tooling: Browser only. Support channels named on the FAQ: help2.turboget.net, online chat, email [address removed], Skype roman.Turbobit.net, ICQ 574295970.
chaining: A second front door to the same Turbo codes sold by turbobitpremium.org and by the Russian forum resellers; useful only if its price or its payment rail differs, which could not be read.

limits.value: the whole tariff grid is client-side rendered; the price is not in the HTML

limits_note: No numeric limit could be read, so none is recorded.
binding_note: Nothing could be measured. The record exists because the domain is a Turbobit-operated storefront, not because a constraint was found; naming a binding here would be a guess.

identity_cost.detail: The FAQ describes buying as a guest ('you will receive a Turbo (premium) code') or into an account; the checkout could not be read, so the exact fields are unverified.

reliability_note: The FAQ is a copy of Turbobit's own FAQ (it opens 'What is Turbobit.net?') and support runs on turbobit.net addresses, so a buyer is dealing with the Turbobit operator through a second domain; nothing about that is disclosed on the home page.
confidence_note: The service exists and is a Turbobit storefront - that part is documented. The price, the payment methods and the traffic allowance are not readable: /tariffs, /prices and /premium all answer 200 with an empty SPA shell. A rendered session would raise this to documented.

evidence.proved: the FAQ is Turbobit's own ('What is Turbobit.net?'), the guest Turbo-code purchase path, and the support addresses @Turbobit.net
